extracted.intended_audience: undergraduate fiction students (UCSB ENG 193) / college creative-writing students
extracted.subtask_description: A college-level grading rubric for short fiction assignments describing the qualities expected for A–F ranges (prose, plot, character, genre engagement, etc.). Designed to guide student writers and TAs on what earns each grade band.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-predictable plot lines
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A-level stories avoid predictability; predictable endings are listed as an issue that prevents A-level. Related B/C/D descriptions show progressively weaker plot expectations (coherent plot for B, unclear narrative arc for C, disjointed narrative structure for D).

rubrics_metrics.name: Believable characters
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characters should feel real and credible. Anti-patterns include flat characterization (B-level problem), underdeveloped characters (C-level), and unbelievable characterization (D-level). Character consistency is expected at B; loss of believability lowers the grade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong familiarity with genre conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: "Strong familiarity with genre conventions (e.g., detective fiction)" (A-range bullet).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Genre engagement is criterial throughout: A and B require demonstrated understanding; C includes failure to satisfy genre conventions; D indicates minimal genre fit. Meeting conventions while also bringing freshness is valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satisfying resolution
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An A-level story provides a resolution that feels earned and satisfying. Predictable or unsatisfying endings are cited as reasons a story falls short of A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genuine reader enjoyment
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A stories should produce clear enjoyment for the reader; the rubric contrasts this with 'extreme lack of engagement' at the D level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original premise or fresh treatment of familiar premise
rubrics_metrics.description: "Original premise or fresh treatment of familiar premise" (A-range bullet).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Originality or a novel take on a known trope helps earn A-range grades. Lack of originality can contribute to predictability or flatness noted in lower ranges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentence-level mastery / engaging prose
rubrics_metrics.description: "Sentence-level mastery" and "smart, articulate, and written in engaging prose" (A-range items).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-level control of sentence craft and prose voice is required for A. B expects 'basically solid, engaging prose'; C includes 'awkward writing' and persistent grammatical problems (C+ is the ceiling for such issues); D includes severe writing flaws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherent plot
rubrics_metrics.guidance: B-level work should have an intelligible, coherent plot even if it lacks the originality or unpredictability of A work. Coherence degrades into 'unclear narrative arc' (C) or 'disjointed narrative structure' (D).

rubrics_metrics.name: Character consistency
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characters should act in ways consistent with established traits and motivations. Inconsistency contributes to lower grades (e.g., flat or underdeveloped characters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrates understanding of genre
rubrics_metrics.guidance: B-level stories show knowledge of genre expectations even if they do not push them as successfully as A work; failure to engage the genre drops the piece to C or D.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issues preventing A-level (flat characterization, predictable endings, inadequate setting, uneven pacing)
rubrics_metrics.description: B-range note listing common problems that keep a piece from A: "flat characterization, predictable endings, inadequate setting, uneven pacing."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are specific anti-patterns: each can lower a story from A to B or below. Use as diagnostic checklist when improving work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic engagement with story expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: "Basic engagement with story expectations" (C-range opening line).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C-level work meets only minimal story expectations — it is engaged but flawed in craft or execution. The rubric lists typical C shortcomings that define this ceiling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awkward writing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awkwardness in style and sentence construction undermines clarity and engagement; persistent grammatical problems cap a piece at C+.

rubrics_metrics.name: Underdeveloped characters
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characters lacking development, motivation, or depth keep a story from higher grades; contrasted with 'believable characters' in A-range.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unclear narrative arc
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the sequence of events or the story's trajectory is unclear, the piece cannot reach B or A; this can devolve into 'disjointed narrative structure' at D.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unconvincing dialogue
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dialogue that fails to reveal character, advance plot, or read naturally hurts the story's credibility and engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to satisfy genre conventions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not meeting the basic expectations of the chosen genre prevents higher grades; genre engagement is a recurring, criterial element across grade bands.

rubrics_metrics.name: C+ ceiling for persistent grammatical problems
rubrics_metrics.description: "C+ is the ceiling for stories with persistent grammatical problems" (explicit scoring note).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Persistent grammar issues impose a hard cap on grade even if other elements are present; remediate grammar to move above C+.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamental craft absent (D-range)
rubrics_metrics.description: D-range: "At least one fundamental problem preventing satisfactory basic-level operation" (e.g., minimal genre fit, severe writing flaws, unbelievable characterization, disjointed narrative structure, extreme lack of engagement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any single severe deficiency in craft or engagement can drop a story to D. This level indicates the piece fails to operate as a basic short story in its form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism or profoundly inappropriate response (F)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These earn an F and may carry institutional penalties beyond the grade. Treat as separate from craft-based failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency and grammatical control separate B/C boundary
rubrics_metrics.description: "The line between B and C is consistency and grammatical control" (from 'What This Rubric Reveals').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if a story shows ideas and genre understanding, inconsistent execution or lack of grammatical control will keep it in the C range rather than B.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prose + character believability + plot non-predictability define A/B boundary
rubrics_metrics.description: "The line between A and B is prose + character believability + plot non-predictability" (from 'What This Rubric Reveals').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To move from a good (B) story to an excellent (A) one, strengthen sentence-level craft, make characters fully believable, and avoid predictable plotting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamental craft presence defines C/D boundary
rubrics_metrics.description: "The line between C and D is whether fundamental craft is present at all" (from 'What This Rubric Reveals').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If basic storytelling craft (clear arc, readable prose, plausible characters, genre engagement) is missing, the piece falls to D.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre engagement is criterial throughout
rubrics_metrics.description: "Genre engagement is criterial throughout" (final rubric statement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every grade band references genre: strong familiarity for A, demonstrated understanding for B, failure to satisfy conventions for C, and minimal fit for D. Choosing and meeting genre expectations is essential.
